The tweet claims to show devastation from an Iranian missile strike 'last night' in Bat Yam, Tel Aviv. Snopes and multiple fact-checkers confirmed this video is from the June 2025 Iranian missile strike on Bat Yam during the Twelve-Day War, not from March 2026. The March 2026 Iranian strikes hit different areas, not Bat Yam. This is a clear case of old footage being recycled with a false timestamp.

While the White House has not ruled out a draft, Congress has not authorized one. Multiple sources (Poynter, Fox, NewsNation) confirm no draft exists. The accompanying video appears to be AI-generated satire, not real footage.

Reuters reported Iran was nearing a deal to buy CM-302s, but China officially denied any finalized deal or delivery. While some outlets report possible transfers, independent verification is lacking and China's Foreign Ministry explicitly denied it. The claim that missiles were launched and all failed is unverified by credible sources.

While there have been clashes between US forces and Iran-backed Iraqi militias, and US airstrikes on militia targets, these are not 'heavy battles between Iraqis and US forces' in the conventional sense. The fighting involves militia groups, not the Iraqi military proper, and the scale described is exaggerated compared to Reuters and other reporting on the actual incidents.

Multiple fact-checkers (Poynter, Lead Stories, Haaretz, CNN) confirmed that AI-generated videos of Iranian missile strikes on Tel Aviv have gone viral with millions of views. The video's cartoonish imagery, music overlay, and fireworks-like effects are hallmarks of AI generation. Hive AI detection tool gave 99% probability of being digitally created.
